slides.title: TRIBE: Predicting Team Performance via Communication Behavior Ensembles
slides.tldr: PREDICTING TEAM PERFORMANCE VIA COMMUNICATION PATTERNS
slides.highlight: TRIBE uses communication patterns to categorize teams into performance-predictive behavioral tribes, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception of hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: TRIBE predicts team performance by clustering communication patterns, enabling interventions as early as 10% task completion.
card.key_idea: A domain-independent pipeline using topic modeling (NMF/LDA) and clustering (GMM/K-means) to categorize teams into performance-predictive 'behavioral tribes' based on interaction transcripts.
card.evaluation: Tested on four datasets (Minecraft, DELI, GAP); used adjusted R², ANOVA, and Cohen's d. Results show strong predictive power, especially in high-behavioral-freedom tasks.
card.limitation: Predictive effectiveness depends on the task structure's capacity to allow for behavioral variation and expression.

slides.title: Designing Social Robots for Inclusive Child Wellbeing Assessment: Insights from Communities Supporting Developmental Language Disorder and Forced Migration
slides.highlight: This research provides design recommendations for using social robots to assess the wellbeing of children with communication barriers, supporting the RwB focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Design guidelines for inclusive social robot-mediated wellbeing assessments for children with communication barriers and forced migration backgrounds.
card.key_idea: Used design probes and focus groups with parents and professionals to identify ethical and inclusive requirements for robot-led activities targeting language, social, and emotional behaviors.
card.evaluation: Thematic analysis of focus group discussions with 14 stakeholders (parents and professionals) across DLD and forced migration contexts.
card.limitation: The study relies on stakeholder perspectives rather than direct interaction data from children.

slides.title: Deep Learning for Real-Time Sound Order Recognition in Human-Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: REAL-TIME SOUND ORDER RECOGNITION FOR HRI
slides.highlight: This research introduces a deep learning framework to recognize the temporal order of overlapping sounds, which is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A deep learning framework for real-time recognition of the temporal order of overlapping non-verbal sounds.
card.key_idea: A multi-branch CNN processing Mel spectrograms, MFCCs, and STFT features, utilizing an attention-based fusion mechanism to identify sound sequences.
card.evaluation: Tested on synthetic overlaps (same/varied amplitude, unseen sounds); achieved 99% accuracy for balanced overlaps and 74% for unseen data.
card.limitation: Experiments relied on carefully controlled synthetic overlaps, raising concerns regarding ecological validity and deployment in real-room environments.

slides.title: Graphing the Everyday: A Neurosymbolic Approach to Eliciting Routines for Just-In-Time Adaptive Interventions
slides.highlight: This work explores a neurosymbolic pipeline combining LLMs and knowledge graphs to map verbal narratives into routines, supporting MIMIC's focus on neuro-symbolic and LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: A neurosymbolic pipeline for JITAIs that maps unstructured user narratives into structured knowledge graphs for routine elicitation.
card.key_idea: Combines LLMs with a Neo4j knowledge graph and state-machine governance to translate fluid verbal descriptions of daily routines into actionable, structured schedule data.
card.evaluation: Qualitative lab study with 16 participants using natural-language playbacks, state-machine traces, and knowledge-graph visualizations to assess representational fidelity.
card.limitation: A "mental-model gap" exists where linear LLM extraction fails to capture hierarchical, non-linear human storytelling, causing entity fragmentation.

slides.title: High Fidelity Capture, Reconstruction, and Transfer of Human Demonstrations for Robot-Assisted Bathing
slides.tldr: FRAMEWORK FOR CAPTURING AND TRANSFERRING CONTACT-RICH BATHING DEMONSTRATIONS
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework for capturing high-fidelity human bathing demonstrations to improve physical human-robot interaction, supporting RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: A framework for capturing and transferring high-fidelity human bathing demonstrations to a robot-assisted system.
card.key_idea: Uses contact regions as processing primitives to reconstruct synchronized motion, shape, and force, enabling retargeting to a soft robotic hand and arm via open- and closed-loop control.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using a dataset of 128 captures (3 clinicians, 6 subjects) and real-world testing on a mannequin; closed-loop control reduced unsafe pressures.
card.limitation: Substantial sim-to-real gap; lacks shear force data; cannot yet handle real-time human pose changes or non-static bodies.

slides.title: DOBOT Unveils All-Terrain Humanoid Robot LUMO
slides.tldr: ALL-TERRAIN HUMANOID ROBOT WITH VR TELEOPERATION
slides.highlight: The introduction of the LUMO all-terrain humanoid robot and its VR teleoperation capabilities is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: Toward Resilient Human-AI Collaboration: A Lifecycle Taxonomy of Sociotechnical Risks and Cascading Failures
slides.tldr: SOCIOTECHNICAL RISK TAXONOMY FOR HUMAN-AI COLLABORATION
slides.highlight: This paper identifies recurring risk clusters in human-AI collaboration, such as trust miscalibration and cognitive burden, which is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception of hybrid team states.

card.one_liner: A lifecycle-based taxonomy of sociotechnical risks that undermine human-AI collaboration across diverse professional domains.
card.key_idea: Synthesizes fragmented literature into a four-stage lifecycle (allocation, interaction, feedback, adoption) and six recurring risk clusters to model how failures cascade.
card.evaluation: Conceptual synthesis of existing literature across five domains (healthcare, journalism, education, management, defense); no new empirical datasets used.
card.limitation: The framework is a conceptual interaction model providing a foundation for future empirical validation rather than tested results.

slides.title: Robot Learning from Human Demonstrations: Handwritten Alphabet Trajectories and Human-Likeness Evaluation
slides.tldr: LEARNING HUMAN-LIKE ROBOT MOTION FROM HANDWRITING DEMONSTRATIONS
slides.highlight: This work presents a framework for learning human-like robot motion from handwriting demonstrations, which is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied learning.

card.one_liner: A framework for learning human-like robot handwriting using an extended GMM+GMR approach and a new dataset.
card.key_idea: Extends GMM+GMR by incorporating contact force and normalized time dimensions and implementing segment-wise processing to handle non-continuous, multi-stroke trajectories.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via a user study (21 participants) using a simulated UR10 robot; achieved a mean human-likeness score of 71.50/100.
card.limitation: Used simulated robots instead of physical hardware; small participant sample sizes; linear interpolation for pen-lift transitions; no pen orientation data.

slides.title: From Speech to Interaction: Analyzing Multimodal Systems in Cocktail-Party Scenarios
slides.highlight: This work analyzes multimodal systems for recognizing speaker groups and transcribing conversations in cocktail-party scenarios, which is relevant to HyECHO's focus on identity recognition and diarization in hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: Analysis of multimodal systems for cocktail-party speech recognition, showing that AVSR modeling drives performance more than speech separation.
card.key_idea: Evaluates three strategies for multi-party transcription and clustering: audio-visual target speech separation, improved AVSR backbones, and LLM-based semantic grouping of conversations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the CHiME-9 MCoRec dataset using WER, Clustering F1, and Joint Error; best system achieved 57% relative error reduction.
card.limitation: Semantic clustering depends on transcription quality, and visual interaction cues (like gaze) generalize poorly compared to LLM-based reasoning.
